title: Atoms and Alchemy: Chymistry and the Experimental Origins of the Scientific Revolution (publisher page)
ask_addressed: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? Which links are documented in texts and manuscripts?
quote: exposes the speciousness of these views and challenges widely held beliefs about the origins of the Scientific Revolution.
summary: Publisher's description: Newman traces the alchemical roots of Boyle's mechanical philosophy and names the medieval Geber among Boyle's predecessors. The blurb asserts Newman's thesis; it does not show the textual links.
limits: Publisher blurb, promotional; the argument itself was not read. Stance lowered from supports to context: the page does not document a text-by-text transmission chain. Year (2006) is the page's copyright line.

title: Alchemy Tried in the Fire (publisher page)
authors: Newman, W. R.; Principe, L. M.
ask_addressed: What does the historiography (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) say about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era?
quote: Winner of the 2005 Pfizer Prize from the History of Science Society.
summary: Records the book's recognition by the History of Science Society and its framing around Boyle's work with the alchemist Starkey.
limits: Prize notice and blurb only; does not itself argue continuity beyond the framing. Year 2002 not re-checked on the page.

title: The Secrets of Alchemy (publisher page)
ask_addressed: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? Which links are documented in texts and manuscripts?
quote: traces the genealogy of alchemical practices from their early Greco-Egyptian foundations through early modern chymistry
summary: Table of contents runs Greco-Egyptian chemeia, Arabic al-Kimiya, Medieval Latin alchemia, then early modern chymistry: a scholar's own chain of transmission. The quote is a blurb on the page.
limits: Table of contents and blurbs only; the chain's evidence is in the book, not read. Promotional.

title: Robert of Chester's Liber de compositione alchemiae (Wikipedia)
ask_addressed: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? Which links are documented in texts and manuscripts?
quote: generally considered to be the first Latin translation of an Arabic work on alchemy into Latin, completed on 11 February 1144
summary: Dates the Latin translation, notes the falsely attributed Khalid ibn Yazid and the Byzantine monk Morienus, a pupil of Stephanus of Alexandria: a textual link from Alexandria to Arabic to Latin.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Whether the dialogue's Byzantine/Alexandrian lineage is historical is not settled by this page.

title: Alchemy in the medieval Islamic world (Wikipedia)
ask_addressed: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? Which links are documented in texts and manuscripts?
quote: are also known to have been practiced by pre-Islamic Alexandrian alchemists.
summary: Notes that al-Razi's laboratory operations (calcination, distillation, etc.) overlap with those of Alexandrian alchemists and that the Khalid-Marianos teacher story is regarded as legend by Ullmann.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Rhazes-specific scholarship (e.g. Ferrario on genuine vs. pseudo-Razi texts) was found in search but not opened.

title: Emerald Tablet (Wikipedia)
ask_addressed: What does the historiography (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) say about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era?
quote: It is believed to have been compiled in Arabic in the late eighth or early ninth century.
summary: Earliest source is the Arabic Secret of Creation, c. 8th-9th century, compiled partly from earlier Greek or Syriac material; so no pharaonic-era attestation.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Contradicts the pharaonic-age claim only; Kraus and Weisser are cited, not read.

title: Hermetica (Wikipedia)
ask_addressed: What does the historiography (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) say about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era?
quote: both were products of complex interactions between Greek and Egyptian culture.
summary: Reports Fowden's view that philosophical and technical Hermetica are Greek-Egyptian products, Bull (2018) arguing Egyptian priests wrote them in Greek in late Ptolemaic and Roman times, and the c. 100-300 CE dating.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Texts are Roman-era Greek, so not pharaonic; but Egyptian priestly input is argued, so the picture is mixed, not one-sided. Fowden and Bull themselves not read.

quote: Much of what are known as Isaac Newton's occult studies can largely be attributed to his study of alchemy.
summary: Establishes that alchemy occupied Newton; says nothing on Egyptian origin.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Lavoisier not covered by any opened source. Quote verified in the page's raw wikitext (rendered page rate-limited).

title: George G. M. James (Wikipedia; the Stolen Legacy URL shows this article)
ask_addressed: What does the historiography (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) say about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? quote: Stolen Legacy and its thesis have generally been considered pseudohistory by historians.
summary: Sceptical record on the 'Greek learning is Egyptian' thesis (G. G. M. James 1954); an analogue to the 'chemistry is Egyptian science' claim, not a rebuttal of it.
limits: Wikipedia (tertiary); use as a pointer to the scholarship it cites, not as evidence in itself. Does not address chemistry or alchemy specifically. Page title differs from the URL name.
